title: LinkIdentity
description: The body of a request to link an external identity to the caller's own account, derived from identity_application::accounts::LinkIdentity. `state` is the one-time code Identity issued to the client for the CSRF binding, and it is what proves this callback belongs to this session.
x-serde-status: the type is IMPLEMENTED as a shape; LinkIdentityCommand has no body and no route serves it

provider.description: Which provider asserted it. The subject is only stable WITHIN a provider, which is why the two travel together: two providers may mint the same subject string, and treating either as globally unique on its own is an account-takeover primitive.

x-accepted-values.reserved: saml — a declared variant because the domain is expected to need it, not because anything implements it. Linking a SAML identity is not in the roadmap at all; adding it would be a new phase.

subject.description: The provider's identifier for the user. Bounded at 512 bytes by Identity::new so a hostile provider cannot write an unbounded row. The pairing (provider, subject) is the natural key and is the subject of the 'user subject cannot be reused' invariant.

state.description: The one-time state that binds the provider's callback to THIS session. A mismatch is a refusal, and it is the only thing standing between an attacker's callback and a link on the victim's account.

x-on-refusal.already-linked-elsewhere: ApplicationError::Domain. The refusal MUST be explicit. Silently no-op'ing would leave the user believing a link exists that does not, and the (provider, subject) pair stays attached to the account that already holds it — re-attaching it to a different user is the account-takeover shape this command exists to make hard to write.
x-on-refusal.phase: Phase 5 — Applications, grants, and the self-service surface
